rules.title: General
items: Vanguard-related work comes first. This is NOT a Vanguard function and no activities associated with this league are related to Vanguard.
18 teams, 2 players per team. Rounds are played on Wednesday evenings; first tee time 4:10 PM.
All returning players start the season with their final round (Round 18) handicap from last season.
There are 18 regular season rounds plus 3 playoff rounds. All rounds canceled due to weather will not be rescheduled.
Week 18 is the Knockdown Round — pairings based on current standings (1v2, 3v4, 5v6, etc.). The Tie Rule is in effect. There is no rain-out round.
A round is considered official if the final team has finished the 6th hole. For H7 use H1 score, H8 use H4 score, H9 use H3 score.
One-time non-refundable membership fee: $60.00/season payable to Krista (Treasurer). All members must be paid in full by Week 10 or the team is ineligible for playoffs.
Green fees (subject to change): Walking $25.00 · Walking with hand cart $27.00 · Riding $36.00.
If you cannot play, it is your responsibility to arrange a substitute. Missing 3 rounds without a substitute = subject to expulsion pending League Commissioner Committee vote.
The top 8 teams make the playoffs.
Only the winning team's last name can be engraved on the league trophy — no substitutes or replacements.

rules.title: Scoring (Adjusted Stableford)
items: Double Eagle = 5 points
Eagle = 4 points
Birdie = 3 points
Par = 1 point
Bogey = 0 points
Double Bogey = −1 point
Match points: 2 points awarded per head-to-head competition (low handicap vs. low handicap / high handicap vs. high handicap).

rules.title: Bonus Points
items: Bonus points are awarded each week once all 9 matches are scored, based on total combined Stableford scoring.
Top 2 teams (and ties): +8 bonus pts
Next 2 teams (and ties): +6 bonus pts
Next 2 teams (and ties): +4 bonus pts
Last 2 teams (and ties): +2 bonus pts
The lowest 7 rounds of the entire season are used to calculate handicaps for all members.
Returning players — all rounds played at 90%. No staggered percentages.
Returning players — handicap cannot increase more than 2 strokes from the previous season's final handicap (cap applies until they shoot low enough to come back down).
New members — 60% for the first 7 rounds played, then 90% from Round 8 onward. Starting handicap is set from the calculated (60%) result of their first round.
Substitute player points: 6 Stableford points (flat). Handicaps are not calculated for subs.
Phantom sub plays with a 12 handicap and scores double bogey on every hole = 2 Stableford points. A phantom counts as a strike against the full-time player's membership eligibility.
Handicaps can be negative. The lowest (easiest) holes will reduce par to allow for a negative handicap.
Playoff subs must use their standard full-time league player handicap. No deduction of points.
Stroke Index (SI) order: 1, 3, 7, 8, 4, 9, 2, 6, 5.
rules.title: Handicaps
Player of the Year
items: WEEKLY: Highest individual point-getter for the week receives a cash payout. Ties split the payout equally.
YEARLY: Highest individual point-getter for the entire season is crowned Player of the Year.
Yearly calculation: throw out the 3 lowest scores, then sum the rest.
If a sub or phantom score is not one of the low 3, that point total is included. If a player has a sub for 5 weeks, the sub total counts twice.
Cash payouts (weekly and yearly) are determined based on league membership count.
Tee times are assigned to each group weekly. First tee time: 4:10 PM.
No guaranteed tee times are accepted throughout the year.
All tee times and matches are distributed at the beginning of the season as part of the schedule.
All teams must play in their scheduled time slots unless approved by commissioners.
If a player must make up holes, the opposing player can replay the hole or keep their original score — if replayed, that score is final.
Any round not played on Wednesday night must be played with a member of the opposite team so the round is attested by the opponent.
rules.title: Tee Times

items: All membership and substitute eligibility is voted on by the Rules Committee. All decisions are final.
Playoff eligibility: all members must play at least 66% of the regular season (calculation rounded up). Failure = team is ineligible for playoffs.

Playoff matches are expected to be played as scheduled. Unplanned rescheduling requires Rules Committee approval within 24 hours. Rescheduled matches must be completed before the next scheduled playoff round.
Playoff subs must be a fully paid regular league member who did not qualify for playoffs but met the 66% eligibility requirement. Sub uses their league handicap — no deduction, no max points.
Teams choosing not to use a playoff sub will use the phantom sub rules as in the regular season.
League membership is subject to committee review each year.
rules.title: Eligibility

items: Playoff seed is based on finish in the regular season (includes Week 18 Knockdown Round).
Round 1 (Quarterfinals): 1v8, 2v7, 3v6, 4v5.
Round 2 (Semifinals): highest remaining seed vs. lowest remaining seed.
Finals: Championship match + 3rd Place match. League party follows.
All playoff ties: sudden death starting at Hole 1.
rules.title: Playoffs
Regular Season Tie Breakers
items: Tie breaker 1: Head-to-head match result from the season. If tied or teams didn't play each other, proceed to TB2.

Tie breaker 2: Pull the scorecard from each team's match against the 1st-place team (follow down the standings to find a common playoff-qualified opponent). Highest total points from that match (excluding bonus) wins the spot.
If still tied: random pick.
Two teams tied for 8th seed: 3-hole match play. If still tied: sudden death. If still tied: coin toss.
Three teams tied for 8th: apply tie-breaker order — top team gets a bye while other two play sudden death; winner plays the bye team sudden death.
Three teams tied for 7th: apply tie-breaker order — top team is seeded 7th; remaining two play a 3-hole match play for 8th.
The Rules Committee/Commissioners will make fair and unbiased determinations for scenarios not covered above.
All disputes must be logged within 24 hours to Chris Coyne, Jack Carickhoff, and Brian Charles.
The Rules Committee's decisions are final.
All other situations not covered by these rules follow USGA rules and interpretations.
rules.title: Disputes

items: Hole #1: Drives landing right of the tree line bordering the driving range are out of bounds (safety rule). Penalized one stroke, play from the spot where the ball crosses the tree line.
Hole #2: Tee shot landing inside the tree line on the right side is in play. If the ball is lost, stroke and drop apply — no closer to the hole.
Hole #5: Drives going into the road from the tee are out of bounds. Stroke and drop, no closer to hole. Ball must be dropped on the right side of the trees.

Hole #8: Ball ending in the second water hazard — drop area is between the ponds. No cutting the corner from the tee (tee shot left of the second pond, closer to the hole) = 2-stroke penalty. If without question the ball entered the pond from the fairway, play along the line of entry with a 1-stroke penalty.
rules.title: Course Rules — Hole by Hole

items: Lost balls (not otherwise specified): 1-stroke penalty, continue from approximate location where ball was lost.
Balls hit into the woods may be played out of the woods with no penalty. Alternatively, play from the point of entry into the woods with a 1-stroke penalty (e.g., Hole #12 hook into the woods).
Tee box rule: if you tee off from a tee box (white or gold), you cannot move up to an easier tee box during the season. You are allowed to move back if necessary.

Sand trap: you may rake the area underneath your ball and replace it in the same spot. You cannot move the ball to a new location. If the ball is in water in the trap, you may move it to a new location within the trap, no closer to the hole.
Wet conditions / rain: you have the option to lift, clean, and replace your ball.
Search time: players have a full 3 minutes to identify their ball. The opposing team may start a timer and instruct a drop after 3 minutes have expired.
If you tee off in certain tee box (white or gold), you can't move up to another tee-box. You are allowed to move back if necessary.

18.note:
The Field Is Set
The regular season is officially over, and the PVGC playoff field is locked. Pineno-MacKenzie didn’t just hold onto first place—they stomped on the gas, crushing Charles-Dagg 35-20 in the biggest matchup of the season. West-Herman surged into third, four teams finished within 14 points of each other from fourth through seventh, and the final eight-team playoff field is now set.

And perhaps most importantly: the commissioner has successfully avoided having to explain the playoff format.

For now.

Before we get into the commentary, reminder that everyone is welcome to play this week. The playoff groups will start at 4:30. That leaves the 4:10 and 4:20 times open. Just make your own foursome, and let Jimmy know. Do not contact me with your foursome, I truly don’t need to know! Just Jimmy! You can also go after the playoff times. Would definitely not recommend that, as this is going to be some slow golf!!!



🏆 Match Commentary
Pineno - MacKenzie def. Charles - Dagg (35-20)
Well, that’s one way to win the regular-season championship.

Scot Pineno and Scott MacKenzie absolutely detonated in the biggest match of the night, combining for a ridiculous 35 Stableford points. MacKenzie led the way with 18, while Pineno added 17, and suddenly the two Scotts have gone from chasing Charles-Dagg to finishing the regular season with a 12-point cushion at the top.

Brian Charles and Karl Dagg were certainly respectable with 12 and eight, but this wasn’t a night for respectable. Pineno-MacKenzie have officially earned the No. 1 seed—and everyone else now gets to try to figure out how to stop them.

West - Herman def. Fahey - Wzorek (31-18)
West-Herman entered the night sitting fourth and left it sitting third.

Jack West posted 13 Stableford points, but Ron Herman stole the show with an enormous 18-point performance. Chris Fahey and Barry Wzorek combined for 18, which normally sounds like a pretty good team score—until the other side puts up 31.

The victory moves West-Herman to 148 points and gives them a very favorable playoff position. Fahey-Wzorek, meanwhile, slip to fourth and will now have to deal with Saenz-Huston in the quarterfinals.

Brosius - Albano tied Saenz - Huston (19-19)
This one was about as even as it gets.

Steve Brosius and Mike Albano combined for 19, while Bob Saenz and Dennis Huston matched them exactly. Saenz won the individual battle against Brosius, while Albano answered by taking down Huston. Basically, everyone got a win, everyone got a loss, and nobody got to complain about the result.

Brosius-Albano finish the regular season in seventh, while Saenz-Huston hold onto fifth. And because the standings are apparently determined by a random-number generator disguised as a golf league, these two teams could meet again in the semifinals.

Carickhoff - Schantz def. Glascott - Adler (18-11)
Jack Carickhoff continues his campaign to make 38 look like a bad round.

Jack posted another excellent score, this time a 38, while Tracy Schantz came through with 11 Stableford points to lead Carickhoff-Schantz to the victory. Scott Glascott and Mark Adler combined for only 11, bringing their regular season to an end at 125 points.

The win was especially important for Carickhoff-Schantz, who climb to sixth and earn a quarterfinal matchup against third-seeded West-Herman. Jack’s 38 also gives him another appearance in the Low Gross department, because apparently that’s just what he does now.

Harvey - Rowles def. Lukas - Blizard (15-11)
John Harvey and Jeff Rowles closed out the regular season with a solid victory.

Jeff posted 10 Stableford points and handled Carol Blizard’s substitute with relative ease, while Harvey and Rhonda Lukas tied their individual matchup at five apiece. It wasn’t flashy, but Harvey-Rowles did exactly what they needed to do and moved into the eighth and final playoff spot.

That means the No. 1 seed Pineno-MacKenzie now gets to deal with the team that just squeaked into the postseason.

No pressure, guys.

Franks - Lightbody def. Mistry - Reddy (19-13)
Scott Lightbody was nowhere to be found this week.

And by “nowhere to be found,” we mean officially a phantom.

John Franks apparently decided that was his cue to take over, firing a 40 raw and 17 Stableford points to lead Franks-Lightbody to the win. Baz Mistry still had a respectable 11, but Sanjay Reddy’s phantom score left Mistry-Reddy unable to keep pace.

Franks-Lightbody finish tenth, while Mistry-Reddy close out the regular season in 12th. And after Lightbody’s recent run of spectacular scores, it’s probably fitting that the one week he doesn’t play is the week his team wins.

Lorenz - Huckestein def. Posey - Minasian (19-16)
Gabe Lorenz finally decided to remind everyone that he can actually play this game.

His 13 Stableford points were the difference as Lorenz-Huckestein edged Posey-Minasian. Jake Huckestein’s substitute contributed six, while Russ Posey and Aret Minasian combined for 16.

Lorenz-Huckestein finish the season in 13th, while Posey-Minasian land at 14th. Neither team made the playoffs, but at least Gabe got to end the regular season with a win instead of another double-digit Stableford disaster.

Pavelik - Mitchell def. Mulvey - Nelson (18-11)
Barry Pavelik carried the entire operation.

His 12 Stableford points were more than enough to push Pavelik-Mitchell past Mulvey-Nelson, with Mark Mitchell’s substitute adding six. Chris Nelson did manage to win his individual match, but Tom Mulvey’s four points weren’t nearly enough to keep the team competitive.

Pavelik-Mitchell finish the regular season in 15th, while Mulvey-Nelson finish 16th. Somewhere, the commissioner is probably already working on a completely unnecessary statistical explanation for why 16th place is actually “competitive.”

Jurden - Olivos def. Wagner - Hammond (11-4)
Jurden-Olivos have officially discovered the concept of momentum.

After spending most of the season at the bottom of the standings, Jesse Jurden and JC Olivos closed things out with their second straight victory, this time beating Wagner-Hammond 11-4. Jesse posted nine points and won his individual match, while the phantom pairing on the other side contributed the league minimum.

Jurden-Olivos finish with three wins and 55 points—respectable enough to avoid the basement. Wagner-Hammond finish 18th, but at least they have plenty of time to prepare their offseason excuses.

🧢 Commissioner’s Corner
THAT’S A WRAP ON THE REGULAR SEASON.

And what a finish.

Pineno-MacKenzie have gone from chasing Charles-Dagg to finishing the regular season with the best record in the league and a 12-point lead. Their 35-point explosion against Charles-Dagg was the perfect exclamation point on an incredible regular season.

Charles-Dagg settle for the No. 2 seed, but they’re still dangerous. West-Herman jumped into third with their win over Fahey-Wzorek, while Fahey-Wzorek and Saenz-Huston both finish at 139 points.

Then things get absolutely ridiculous.

Carickhoff-Schantz: 138.

Brosius-Albano: 137.

Harvey-Rowles: 133.

That’s five teams separated by just six points from fourth through eighth.

The playoff field is set, and there are some serious matchups coming.

🏆 The Quarterfinals
1. Pineno - MacKenzie vs. 8. Harvey - Rowles

The No. 1 seed gets the final playoff qualifier. Pineno-MacKenzie are coming off a 35-point demolition of Charles-Dagg, while Harvey-Rowles are simply happy to be here. That’s usually when things get dangerous.

2. Charles - Dagg vs. 7. Brosius - Albano

Charles-Dagg have spent most of the season at or near the top, but their regular-season finale was a wake-up call. Brosius-Albano have been steadily climbing and are coming off a 23-21 victory over Saenz-Huston before tying them this week. This one could get spicy.

3. Carickhoff - Schantz vs. 6. West - Herman

Jack Carickhoff is shooting low scores like he’s personally offended by the number 40. West-Herman, meanwhile, are one of the hottest teams in the league. This could be the most entertaining quarterfinal on the board.

4. Saenz - Huston vs. 5. Fahey - Wzorek

These two teams finished tied at 139 points, making this the closest seed matchup of the entire bracket. Saenz-Huston have been one of the league’s most consistent teams, while Fahey-Wzorek just lost a huge matchup against West-Herman. Both teams have something to prove.
